summary: In civil space developments, NASA announced it is exploring potential commercial servicing options for the Hubble Space Telescope. Global launch and flight operations remained active as SpaceX launched 27 Starlink satellites from California, India successfully orbited a next-generation navigation satellite, and Virgin Galactic conducted the inaugural flight of its new Delta-class space plane. On the commercial front, satellite maker Argotec raised €50 million to scale small-satellite manufacturing, ESI contracted to supply solar array components for missile defense programs, and European nations initiated funding for offensive in-space capabilities. In military space intelligence, the Pentagon revealed a fiscal year 2026 intelligence budget of $30.9 billion, while the Air Force Research Laboratory announced plans for a $30 million cislunar initiative. For civil leadership and deep-space operations, NASA appointed Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman as deputy director of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, and engineers successfully restored normal contact with Voyager 1 after resolving a brief communications pause. In scientific research, analysis of the rare 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 offered new insights into Mars's early history, and astronomers released updated imagery of the Cat's Head Nebula captured by both the James Webb and Hubble space telescopes. Looking ahead, defense and space analysts should watch for the Air Force Research Laboratory's planned $30 million cislunar project award set for next spring.
